core.title: Bind every exposed frontend journey to an E2E or SMOKE browser spec
core.given: A journey has an exposed entrypoint whose surfaces include the frontend or declare none.
core.when: Always, for every such journey, new or pre-existing (e.g. when specs are written, or a journey is added or its exposure or surfaces change).
core.then: At least one e2e spec (a browser-level test) MUST be bound to that journey through the stack's journey binding and carry a test URN of an end-to-end or smoke kind.
prefer: Add a smoke-flavored e2e spec for the journey at the stack's e2e-test location, bound to the journey with the stack's journey binding and carrying an end-to-end or smoke test URN.
avoid: Counting a unit test that only mentions the journey URN in a string as coverage; it is not an e2e spec and leaves the journey uncovered.
Relying on boundary (route-level) tests alone: they prove each routing decision, not that the journey runs end to end.
Renaming a spec to escape judgment: a test file carrying the stack's journey markers in its header is still judged as an e2e spec.
unless: The journey is internal, or its exposed entrypoint's surfaces exclude the frontend (e.g. backend only): no browser surface, out of scope.
Files in the stack's excluded vendored/generated trees (profile roots.excluded) are never scanned: they are neither judged nor counted as coverage.
core.why: An exposed journey is what a user can start. Route-level rules prove each routing decision; this rule proves the journey runs end to end in a browser.
evidence: For every exposed journey with frontend (or undeclared) surfaces, an e2e spec outside excluded trees exists, bound to the journey with the stack's journey binding and carrying an end-to-end or smoke test URN.
The stack's journey-e2e-coverage check reports no findings for this rule.
verification: Strict disposition, severity 3: every in-scope journey without a qualifying spec is a violation.

Qualifying-spec identification follows the stack's file-to-role assignment (profile roles.assignment): an e2e spec is a file with the stack's e2e naming (profile suffix.e2e_test) run by the stack's test runner (profile tooling.test_runner), OR any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker; the OR is disjunctive, so a misnamed spec cannot escape judgment.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not an e2e spec; it counts neither as coverage nor as suppression of the missing-coverage finding.
Scope of the check: in scope are journeys whose entrypoint is exposed AND whose surfaces include the frontend or declare none; internal journeys and surfaces excluding the frontend are out of scope.
The check cross-references every in-scope journey, new or pre-existing, against journey bindings and test URN kinds, not only changed journeys.
Excluded trees (profile roots.excluded) are never scanned; a candidate spec found only there is ignored, so a journey covered only there is reported as uncovered.

values: exposed frontend journey without a journey-bound e2e or smoke spec

fires: A journey with an exposed entrypoint whose surfaces include the frontend (or declare none) has no e2e spec bound to it via the stack's journey binding.
The only spec bound to such a journey carries no end-to-end or smoke test URN.
An in-scope journey's only candidate e2e spec lives inside an excluded tree: that file is ignored, so the journey has no qualifying spec outside excluded trees.
An in-scope journey is mentioned only by a unit test that names its URN in a string: that is not an e2e spec, so the journey is still uncovered.
doesNotFire: The journey is internal (entrypoint not exposed).
The exposed journey's entrypoint surfaces exclude the frontend (e.g. backend only).
Files inside excluded (vendored/generated) trees are themselves never scanned or judged.

profileRequirements.meaning: How a test file is assigned to the e2e-test (browser-spec) role: the disjunctive identification predicate (e2e naming run by the test runner, OR journey markers in header comments), so a misnamed file is still judged.
profileRequirements.bunValue: browser_spec = a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, OR any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// UserSystemFlow:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:userSystemFlow:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the e2e-test role in this stack.
The name pattern by which conventionally named e2e (browser-level) spec files are identified.
The stack's test runner; a qualifying browser spec is a file of e2e naming executed by this runner.
The syntax by which a spec binds itself to a journey.
The test URN kinds a journey-bound spec may carry to satisfy the end-to-end browser-coverage obligation.
Vendored and generated trees that the check never scans.
Where a journey's e2e/smoke spec is placed, with its conventional name.

bunOnly.text: htmx_e2e_detector reports no findings for this rule.
bunOnly.reason: Detector/validator ids of this one rule are realization details; the core's evidence and verification name the check generically.

bunOnly.reason: The finding string embeds the Bun detector id; the core keeps the finding itself (activation.facts[3]) without the id.

neutralityNotes: The journey model (journey, exposed entrypoint, surfaces) and the platform word 'browser' are treated as stack-neutral shared ATDD vocabulary (journey is already a urn artifact). Everything concrete was pushed to the profile, split according to the key docs: the artifact kind browser_spec (roles.e2e_test.kinds), the disjunctive file-to-role identification predicate — e2e naming run by the test runner OR header journey markers (roles.assignment) — the name pattern **/*.e2e.ts (suffix.e2e_test), the runner Playwright (tooling.test_runner), the '// Journey:' binding (urn.binding.journey), the qualifying test URN kinds (urn.test_kinds#e2e_kinds, proposed — no existing key fits), the spec location (layout.e2e_location), and the never-scanned trees (roots.excluded, one stack-wide list). The detector id htmx_e2e_detector stays bunOnly per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys. Nothing in the obligation itself resisted neutralization; instantiating the core with these profile values plus the two bunOnly items reproduces bun.json exactly.
